instrument: ICE Brent March 2027 call spread, long $110 call / short $130 call (expiry late Jan 2027)
entry_trigger: At market on 6 Nov 2026, March 2027 Brent futures at 94.00; spread premium about 3.00 per barrel (do not enter above 4.00). About 65 spreads so total premium is US$200,000 on the US$10m book. The event arrives as an overnight gap, so no price trigger.
stop: Max loss is the premium paid (2% of account). Exit early if March 2027 Brent futures close below 85.00, or on a signed US-Iran agreement or lifting of the naval blockade. Take profit if March 2027 Brent trades at or above 118.00 before 15 Dec rather than holding for 130.
thesis: The midterm sell-off priced Trump's incentive to deal, but escalation was deferred until after the vote, not cancelled, and a lame-duck president facing an Iran that won't move on its core demands is more likely to restart strikes to force terms than to accept them. A restart returns Brent to the October range (115-118) or above, which the spread captures with loss capped at premium. I put a restart at 60% against roughly 50% implied; at a take-profit of 118 the trade risks 3 to make about 5.
key_factors: Trump saying the war ends "very soon, one way or the other" and hinting at post-midterm strikes; US strike on Qeshm Island 3 Nov; Iran's unchanged conditions; tanker attacks at a near-record rate (UKMTO); Democrats split on a deal (Schumer called the June memorandum surrender); Gulf flows ~75% of pre-war, so a closure is a large supply shock; implied volatility extreme, which makes the spread expensive.
change_mind: A signed agreement or extended ceasefire; Trump lifting the blockade; Trump publicly ruling out further strikes; Gulf exports back to pre-war levels with insurance rates falling; March Brent closing below 85.
vs_consensus: Consensus reads the election as pressure toward a deal and prices Brent ~100, roughly a coin flip between the ~80 deal state and the ~118 no-deal state. I put a restart at 60% versus ~50% implied, and think a Democratic Congress is a weaker peace lobby than assumed because its leadership attacked the last deal as appeasement.
entry_level: 6 Nov 2026 close: the NYMEX BZ March 2027 final settlement (private, em-macro-data; replaces the 94.00 placeholder by correction K002)

entry_trigger: No trade (v1.0 runs unchanged) with pre-committed cut and stop rules. Size N/A: governs the whole v1.0 book. Probability: 65% that v1.0 earns a positive live Sharpe after costs over its first 24 live months.
stop:
Hard stop at 27% or more below the index's live peak (rule 2). Rules, measured on the official month-end v1.0 index from the 1 Nov 2026 live start:
(1) Halve: index 20% or more below its live peak -> halve gross exposure at the next rebalance; restore full exposure once the drawdown is back within 10%.
(2) Stop: 27% or more below its live peak -> close v1.0 entirely at the next rebalance; restart only as a new pre-registered version.
(3) Time: live Sharpe after costs below zero at 24 months -> stop v1.0.
(4) Instrument: capital controls, a closed market, or a managed peg or crawl in a held currency -> drop it at the next rebalance.
(5) Carry-spread review: the long-minus-short carry spread below its 2005-2019 10th percentile at two consecutive month-ends -> a written review within 7 days. No automatic cut.
thesis: v1.0's return comes from the carry premium, which pays steadily and loses heavily in crashes. Its test can't yet tell a good strategy from a mediocre one, so the main danger is staying in a broken strategy out of hope. Limits set in advance, plus a fixed review date, prevent that without reacting to normal drawdowns.
key_factors: carry's crash risk; test Sharpe 0.65 +/- 0.4; worst test drawdown -18%; interest-rate gaps narrowing (US-Mexico gap at a record-low 225bp, a Fed hike expected in December); the daily estimate is unreliable because 9 of 23 instruments lack daily prices, so decisions use the official monthly index.
change_mind: daily prices becoming reliable enough to measure drawdown daily; a pre-registered carry-crash filter passing its test (it would replace rule 5); any planned change to the volatility target or the universe.
vs_consensus: Most carry strategies target volatility and ride out drawdowns with no hard stop. This one commits in advance to a hard stop and a time limit, accepting the risk of exiting just before a recovery (as after 2008, March 2020 and August 2024) in exchange for never deciding in the middle of a loss.

country: Turkey (method applies to any currency classed as managed)
instrument: v1.0 systematic book: volatility floor for managed currencies (override outside the frozen code)
entry_trigger: Adjusts v1.0, takes no new discretionary risk. From the 3 Dec 2026 rebalance, a managed currency's assumed volatility is floored at the median volatility of v1.0's emerging-market currencies, then the book is rescaled to its 10% volatility target. Supersedes D004 rule 4.
stop: Hard stop at 27% or more below the index's live peak (D004 rule 2); D004 rules 1-3 apply to the adjusted book. Review within 7 days if trial T27 fails its criteria, or if the CBRT moves to a genuine free float.
thesis: v1.0 sizes positions by inverse volatility, so a currency whose central bank smooths its price looks safer than it is and gets oversized: TRY is about 96% of capital. Flooring its assumed volatility at a normal emerging-market currency's level sizes it like one, keeping part of the carry while cutting exposure to a sudden devaluation.
key_factors: USD/TRY on a managed path of about 20% a year against 30-35% inflation (Commerzbank, Oct 2026); heavy intervention and reserve sales in 2026; record lows near 50; TRY carry about 33pp; devaluations in 2018 and 2021.
change_mind: the CBRT allowing a genuine float; trial T27 failing; long-run evidence that managed currencies' realised risk, crashes included, matches their measured volatility.
vs_consensus: The consensus expects the managed depreciation to continue smoothly, which suits carry. This decision does not predict a devaluation; it says volatility-based sizing underprices the crash risk.
